transcript.text: While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Our backend load replay shows the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I haven't updated the policy draft yet because the client test was owned by another team, but this is a release-impacting finding: the current draft's 100 requests per minute would break legitimate bulk-import synchronization workflows.

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting security finding. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. The current draft applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which is far too permissive and would leave us vulnerable to credential-stuffing attacks. This finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but it needs to be factored into the final policy before launch.
